summary: Choi et al. 2025 (ACL Findings) ran >2,500 structured LLM debates on five ground-truth-free social topics with proponent, opponent, and neutral (always GPT-4o) agents, manipulating group size (1:2, 2:1, up to 1:8) and 'intelligence' (parameter size, large vs small models from GPT/Claude/Qwen). Neutral agents conform significantly to numerical majorities (chi2=164.839, p<0.001; CR 63.5-72.1% at 2:1 vs 39.4-42.2% at 1:2) and to higher-intelligence sides (chi2=142.285, p<0.001; CR 74.3% when the proponent is the large model vs 39.8% when it is small). Critically, intelligence dominates numbers: one large-model agent against two small-model agents still wins 66.3% of turns, while two small agents against one large win only 42.2%; effect size for intelligence (eta_p2~0.167, large) dwarfs majority size (~0.068, moderate), and more capable evaluators (GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5-turbo) are less swayed by headcount as ratios scale to 1:8. Authors conclude argument quality outweighs quantity. However, every condition exposes the neutral to full 256-token persuasive arguments across 3 turns; there is no bare-answer condition, so the paper cannot discriminate answer-only exposure from rationale-mediated influence (rq1 remains open; Choi only bounds it from the rationale side). Conformity here is evaluator persuasion on opinion topics, not accuracy change on verifiable tasks.
unresolved: Exact per-scenario sample sizes, per-provider breakdowns, and Appendix C ANOVA tables were not extracted; needed only if the note quotes provider-specific magnitudes.

Whether Choi-style conformity dynamics (majority pull, capability dominance, spiral-of-silence capitulation) occur on tasks with verifiable answers remains untested by this paper - the key external-validity bridge for the note's mechanism.
The 'complete agreement' capitulation frequency is reported only qualitatively (Appendix E example); no quantitative rate of minority silence is available in the extracted text.
